questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'What Social Science Studies' refers to.
questions.a: Social Science explores people, places and events: it studies how humans live together, how societies and states organise, how economies work and how the past shapes the present - building on the stories explored in Grades 6 to 8.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'What Social Science Studies'.
questions.a: People, places and events studied together: social science reads society like a text.

questions.q: Under which section is 'What Social Science Studies' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Methods of Studying Society' refers to.
questions.a: Social scientists work with evidence - sources, maps, data and field studies - asking questions of the past and present, comparing viewpoints and reasoning from evidence rather than opinion.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Methods of Studying Society'.
questions.a: Evidence first, opinion later: social science argues with sources and data.

concepts.title: Why Social Science Matters for Citizens

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Why Social Science Matters for Citizens' refers to.
questions.a: Studying society equips citizens to understand rights and duties, judge public policies, respect diversity and participate in democracy; the discipline trains informed, questioning and responsible members of the community.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Why Social Science Matters for Citizens'.
questions.a: Informed citizens are made, not born: social science builds the toolkit.
